title: Product of Array Except Self: prefix x suffix product, no division.
shortTitle: Product of Array Except Self: Prefix x Suffix, No Division
keyPoints: For each index, the except-self product is the product of everything to the left times the product of everything to the right.
A left-to-right pass fills the output with prefix products; a right-to-left pass multiplies in suffix products.
No division is used, so zeros are handled naturally without any special casing.
The output array stores prefix intermediates, and a single suffix scalar is the only extra variable, giving O(1) extra space.
Runs in O(n) time with exactly two passes through the array.
For financial growth factors, use BigDecimal with multiply to keep products exact.
This is the same precompute-and-combine idea behind prefix sums, applied to multiplication.

s1_definition.oneliner: For each index, multiply the product of everything to the left by the product of everything to the right, using two sweeps and no division.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Product of Array Except Self** – produces, for each position, the product of every other element without using division.
- **Prefix product** – a left-to-right sweep fills `output[i]` with the product of all elements strictly before index `i`.
- **Suffix product** – a right-to-left sweep multiplies each `output[i]` by the product of all elements strictly after index `i`.
- **O(n) time, O(1) extra space** – two passes, with the output array holding intermediates and one suffix scalar variable.
- **Zero-safe** – handles any number of zeros correctly without branching, unlike a division-based approach.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India computes, for each contributing factor to Rajesh's portfolio growth multiplier, the combined effect of all the other factors, so it can see how the portfolio would grow if one factor were removed. The trick without dividing is to sweep left to right building the running product of everything before each factor, then sweep right to left building the running product of everything after it, and multiply the two sweeps at each position.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│    Product of Array Except Self: Two-Pass Method         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                          │
│  Array:   [a0,  a1,  a2,  a3]                            │
│                                                          │
│  Pass 1 (left → right, prefix):                          │
│  result: [ 1, a0, a0a1, a0a1a2]                          │
│                                                          │
│  Pass 2 (right → left, suffix):                          │
│  result: [a1a2a3, a0*a2a3, a0a1*a3, a0a1a2*1]           │
│           = each position has product of all others      │
│                                                          │
│  Space: output array + 1 suffix variable = O(1) extra    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Product of Array Except Self asks for, at each position, the product of every other element, without division. You solve it with prefix and suffix products in two passes. In a left-to-right pass, fill each output position with the product of everything before it. In a right-to-left pass, multiply each output by a running suffix product. Prefix times suffix at each position is the product of all elements except that one.

The reason division is banned is sound: dividing the total product by each element breaks when any element is zero and forces ugly zero-counting branches. The prefix-suffix method sidesteps that completely, and handles zeros for free: one zero makes every position zero except the zero's own position, and two or more zeros make everything zero, all without a special branch.

On space, you reuse the output array to hold the prefix intermediates and multiply the suffix in on the fly, so you need no separate suffix array, giving O(1) extra space. For financial growth factors, use BigDecimal so the products stay exact.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, this is used for leave-one-out sensitivity analysis on Rajesh's portfolio, modelling growth as a product of daily factors and computing, for each factor, the combined multiplier of all the others.

Remember one sentence: Sweep left to right for prefix products, sweep right to left multiplying in suffix products, and each position ends up with the product of everything except itself, all without division.
